summary: Botswana is one of Africa’s easiest destinations to enter — citizens of some 100 countries, including the EU, US, UK, most of the Commonwealth and all SADC neighbors, get up to 90 visa-free days, while the remaining nationalities apply through the official eVisa portal or a Botswana mission before traveling.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival, with at least two blank pages for stamps — more if you are combining Botswana with neighboring countries.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission (for example Zambia’s northern neighbors, Kenya or Angola).

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry condition, but private clinics expect payment up front and safari areas are remote — cover including medical evacuation is strongly advisable.

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked, but immigration officers may ask visa-free visitors for evidence of onward travel and accommodation, and airlines sometimes verify a return ticket.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of BWP 10,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) should be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Fresh meat, dairy and some plant products may not be brought in from certain countries under foot-and-mouth controls. Expect disinfectant mats and vehicle checks at internal veterinary fences.
Ivory, rhino horn and other wildlife products are strictly prohibited; drone use requires prior permission from the civil aviation authority.

payments.text: Cards are widely accepted in Gaborone, Maun, Kasane and at lodges, and ATMs are common in towns. Carry pula cash for fuel stations, markets and remote areas, and small US dollar notes if crossing borders on safari.

safety.text: Botswana is one of Africa’s safest and most stable countries. The main risks are practical: wildlife and livestock on unlit roads at night, long distances between fuel stops, and petty theft in urban areas.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Botswana Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: The May-to-October dry season is prime safari time — game concentrates on water sources, the Okavango Delta flood peaks mid-year, and nights are cool; November to April is hot, greener and cheaper.

idp.text: Botswana is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: Botswana is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Botswana yet.

tips.text: Travelers under 18 must carry a certified copy of their full birth certificate in addition to a passport, and minors traveling with one parent or alone may need parental consent letters — checked on entry and exit.
Avoid driving outside towns after dark — elephants, cattle and donkeys on unlit roads cause serious accidents, and distances between fuel stations are long, so refuel whenever you can.
Northern Botswana (Okavango, Chobe, Kasane) is a seasonal malaria area, especially November to April. Use repellent and consider prophylaxis; Gaborone and the south are essentially malaria-free.
Visa-free visitors may spend at most 90 days in Botswana within any 12-month period — extensions beyond your stamped stay are requested at an immigration office before it expires.
Expect veterinary checkpoints on main roads — raw meat and some animal products cannot be carried across foot-and-mouth control fences, and shoes and vehicle wheels may be disinfected.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Botswana?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not — citizens of around 100 countries, including the US, UK, EU members, most Commonwealth states and all SADC neighbors, enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities that do need a visa (including India, China and most of the former Soviet states) apply in advance through the official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.bw) or a Botswana mission; there is no visa on arrival.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Botswana visa-free?
faq.answer: You are normally stamped in for up to 90 days, capped at 90 days in total within any 12-month period. Extensions within the cap can be requested at immigration offices in Gaborone and other towns before your stay expires.

faq.question: Do Indian and Chinese citizens need a visa for Botswana?
faq.answer: Yes — both currently need a visa obtained in advance, most conveniently through the official eVisa portal. Botswana has periodically reviewed its policy toward these markets, so check for updates shortly before booking.

faq.question: What documents do children need to enter Botswana?
faq.answer: All travelers under 18 must carry a certified copy of their full (unabridged) birth certificate along with their passport. Minors traveling with one parent, or unaccompanied, should also carry consent letters from the absent parent(s). The rules mirror South Africa’s and are enforced.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Botswana?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from or transit through a yellow fever risk country. Coming directly from Europe, North America or South Africa, no certificate is needed.

faq.question: Can I visit Victoria Falls from Botswana?
faq.answer: Yes — Kasane is about 80 km from the falls, and day trips cross into Zimbabwe (Kazungula road border) or Zambia (Kazungula Bridge). You will pass full immigration both ways, so check the visa rules of Zimbabwe or Zambia for your passport (the KAZA UniVisa, when on sale, covers both).
